A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that changes are confined to pages 1, 5, and 6.

before.justification: v2 reports original data analysis of 60 benchmark leaderboards, including saturation prevalence, comparisons across benchmark properties, parameter sensitivity, and Bayesian regression results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original 60-benchmark analysis, sensitivity results, and appendix case studies and regression results, while revising the public/private subgroup comparison.

M1.justification: The saturation-index procedure, top-five model selection, effective sample-size adjustment, and Bayesian modeling approach remain unchanged. The accessibility-group revision changes the reported data partition rather than the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions analyze the same 60 benchmarks listed in Table 3, with unchanged task, domain, and language coverage. The revised public/private counts concern grouping within this retained collection.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparison method or leaderboard-model set is added or removed. The model entries in Appendix D, Table 6, are identical.

E3.justification: Sections 3.1 and 4.1 and Figure 2 revise the reported accessibility groups from 52 public and 8 private benchmarks to 56 public and 4 private benchmarks. This changes subgroup sizes within the fixed 60-benchmark study; the PDFs do not establish whether other analyses were rerun.

E4.justification: The k/alpha sensitivity analysis in Section 2.3 and Table 1, the five benchmark case studies in Appendix E, and the supplementary regression analyses in Appendix F are unchanged. The H1 revision concerns the primary subgroup comparison.

E5.justification: The uncertainty approximations, significance-reporting practices, standard-deviation error bars, and posterior interval reporting are unchanged. Revised H1 boxplot values do not introduce a different statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 2 updates the public/private saturation distributions, including a visibly narrower private-group interquartile range under the revised grouping. Saturation rates remain approximately 48% for public and 50% for private benchmarks. The overall 29-of-60 high/very-high saturation count, Table 7 values, and appendix regression results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal saturation definition, saturation/stagnation distinction, assumptions, and equations (1)–(4) are identical. No mathematical derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about saturation prevalence, benchmark age and scale, expert curation, and the limited protection offered by private test sets.

C2.justification: The accessibility interpretation still reports no statistically meaningful difference and rejects H1 despite the revised subgroup sizes. The mechanism discussion, recommendations, and Section 6 limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Benchmark-selection instructions, annotation procedures and schema, example model metadata, and code/data access information remain unchanged. The linked repository target is identical.

R1.justification: The references and Appendix A related-work discussion are identical, with no added or removed cited works or substantive change in research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds the University of Hong Kong affiliation for Yu Fan, renumbers subsequent affiliations, and removes the BASIS acronym from an affiliation. Apart from the subgroup-count edits and version stamp, the prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is regenerated with revised H1 displays and adjusted panel dimensions, spacing, and category-label placement. The first-page affiliation block also reflows. Other figures, tables, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revised accessibility counts and Figure 2 may represent a useful correction, but the PDFs do not identify the reclassified benchmarks or explain how the update relates to the unchanged joint regression in Section 4.2 and Appendix F. The private-test-set conclusion also remains unchanged with only four private benchmarks. These omissions prevent a reliable judgment about the revision's effect on analytical consistency and overall quality.
